data.name: Plugin.Description
data.value: Reads hardware sensors and exposes them as Macro Deck variables.

data.name: Configuration.Description
data.value: The sensor window opens in your browser: the Macro Deck 2 dialog, with the whole tree of hardware, reading kind and sensor, the polling rate under it, and a checkbox that asks Windows for administrator rights at every start. Press Continue to open it, and tick the sensors to publish as Macro Deck variables there - what you tick is what is saved. Sensors you leave out stay available from the variable catalog, and the names the Macro Deck 2 plugin used are kept, so an upgraded button keeps working.

data.name: Configuration.WindowRefused
data.value: The sensor window could not be opened in a browser. Press Continue to try again.

data.name: Configuration.WindowLost
data.value: The sensor window closed without sending its selection back. Press Continue to open it again.

data.name: Issues.ReadingsMissing.Elevated
data.value: Elevated readings are on. To have them at every start, tick Start elevated readings at startup in the plugin's settings.

data.name: Issues.ReadingsMissing.ElevationCancelled
data.value: The administrator prompt was dismissed, so the readings that need the driver are still missing.

data.name: Issues.ReadingsMissing.ElevationFailed
data.value: The elevated hardware helper could not be started, so the readings that need the driver are still missing.

data.name: Actions.Sensor.Description
data.value: The fan or pump to control.

data.name: Actions.NoControls
data.value: No controllable fans or pumps were found on this machine.

data.name: Actions.NoControlsBlocked
data.value: No controllable fans or pumps were found. The hardware library's driver is not available to this process, which is what hides them; use Enable elevated readings in Macro Deck's issue list, or start Macro Deck as an administrator, to make them appear.

data.name: Actions.ControlsUnavailable
data.value: The controllable fans or pumps could not be read. The hardware library reported an error.

data.name: Actions.SensorGone
data.value: That fan is no longer present. Pick it again.

data.name: Actions.ControlFailed
data.value: The fan did not accept the change. The hardware library reported an error.

data.name: Actions.SetFanSpeed.Description
data.value: Sets a controllable fan or pump to a percentage of its range. The hardware library's driver must be loaded, which needs the elevated hardware helper or Macro Deck running as administrator.

data.name: Actions.SetFanSpeed.Percent.Description
data.value: Percentage of the fan's own range. 0 is as slow as the chip allows; 100 is full speed.

data.name: Actions.SetFanSpeed.InvalidPercent
data.value: The speed is missing or not a number.

data.name: Actions.RestoreFanControl.Description
data.value: Hands a fan or pump back to the motherboard's own fan curve, undoing a speed set by software.

data.name: Variables.Write.InvalidValue
data.value: The value is missing or not a number.

data.name: Variables.Write.NotFound
data.value: That sensor is no longer known to the plugin.

data.name: Variables.Write.Unavailable
data.value: The sensor cannot be controlled right now. Fan control needs the elevated hardware helper, or Macro Deck running as administrator, with the hardware driver loaded.

data.name: Actions.RestoreAllFans.Description
data.value: Hands every controllable fan and pump back to the motherboard's own curve in one press. Useful as a "silence everything" or shutdown button.

data.name: Actions.RestoreAllFans.Reset
data.value: Every fan and pump was handed back to the motherboard's own control.

data.name: Actions.RestoreAllFans.None
data.value: No controllable fans or pumps were found. The hardware library's driver is either not loaded or not available to this process.

data.name: Actions.RescanHardware.Description
data.value: Re-reads the machine's hardware, so a device attached or removed since Macro Deck started appears without a restart. Software fan speeds are re-applied afterwards.

data.name: Actions.RescanHardware.Failed
data.value: The hardware could not be re-read.

data.name: Variables.Remote.OnlineDescription
data.value: Whether this remote machine is answering. True while it is online, false once it has failed repeatedly.

data.name: Variables.Remote.StatusDescription
data.value: Online, Offline, Reconnecting or Connecting, for a label or a flow condition.

data.name: Variables.Elevated.Description
data.value: Whether the elevated hardware helper is currently reading the driver-backed sensors and driving fans.

data.name: Events.Sensor.Description
data.value: The sensor whose reading the event watches.

data.name: Events.Machine.Description
data.value: The remote machine whose reachability the event watches.

data.name: Events.Threshold.Description
data.value: Starts an automation when a sensor stays above or below a value for a chosen time. The threshold is in the sensor's own unit, for example °C for a temperature.

data.name: Events.Threshold.Direction.Description
data.value: Whether the event is about the reading going up or down.

data.name: Events.Threshold.Limit.Description
data.value: The value the reading is compared with, in the sensor's own unit.

data.name: Events.Threshold.Dwell.Description
data.value: How long the reading has to stay past the threshold before the event fires. Zero fires on the first reading.

data.name: Events.Threshold.Hysteresis.Description
data.value: How far the reading has to come back past the threshold before the event can fire again. Stops a value hovering on the line from firing repeatedly.

data.name: Events.Stopped.Description
data.value: Starts an automation when a sensor has had no reading for a chosen time - a stopped fan, a drive that stopped answering, or a device that went away.

data.name: Events.Stopped.Grace.Description
data.value: How long the sensor may have no reading before the event fires.

data.name: Events.RemoteOffline.Description
data.value: Starts an automation when a configured remote machine stops answering.

data.name: Events.RemoteOnline.Description
data.value: Starts an automation when a remote machine that was offline answers again.

data.name: Events.Elevation.Description
data.value: Starts an automation when the elevated hardware helper starts or stops, which is when the driver-backed readings and fan controls appear or go away.

data.name: Events.Payload.Sensor.Description
data.value: The sensor the event is about.

data.name: Events.Payload.SensorId.Description
data.value: The sensor's stable library identifier, for a flow that needs to tell two sensors with the same name apart.

data.name: Events.Payload.Value.Description
data.value: The reading that crossed the threshold, in the sensor's own unit.

data.name: Events.Payload.Unit.Description
data.value: The unit the value and threshold are in.

data.name: Events.Payload.Machine.Description
data.value: The machine the sensor belongs to.

data.name: Events.Payload.Seconds.Description
data.value: How long the sensor had been without a reading when the event fired.

data.name: Events.Payload.Error.Description
data.value: The last error the remote machine reported.

data.name: Events.Payload.Elevated.Description
data.value: Whether elevated readings are now on.

data.name: Events.SensorsUnavailable
data.value: The sensors could not be read, so there is nothing to pick from.

data.name: Events.NoRemoteMachines
data.value: No remote machines are configured. Add one in the sensor window first.
